rules.rule: Check for urgent features and signs of occupational stress in the health worker
rules.problem: Task lists all 25 identification signs (including non-urgent mood/attendance/performance signs) alongside the red-box urgent items; the page splits these into an urgent box and an identification section, so urgent and non-urgent are mixed in one check_for.

rules.rule: Diagnose possible substance misuse in health worker with occupational stress
rules.problem: Same 19-sign OR list used for all four diagnoses; page only has a single lumped sentence ("any of the above may have..."), with no per-diagnosis mapping, so rules cannot discriminate. Also Stress at work is an added AND gate not on page.

rules.rule: Diagnose possible depression in health worker with occupational stress
rules.problem: Identical condition list to other diagnoses (includes alcohol smell, absenteeism etc.); stress gate not on page. Page supports possible only (may have), which is used correctly.

rules.rule: Diagnose possible anxiety in health worker with occupational stress
rules.problem: As depression rule: undifferentiated condition list and added stress gate. Page says "depression/anxiety" together.

rules.rule: Diagnose possible burnout in health worker with occupational stress
rules.problem: As above; undifferentiated list and added stress gate.

rules.rule: Urgent: health worker with occupational stress and intoxication, inappropriate or aggressive behaviour, or suicidal thoughts

summary: Urgent rule and red-box items are faithful (stress AND any of intoxication, inappropriate behaviour, aggression/violence, suicidal thoughts/plans, correct Urgent level). The four diagnosis rules all share one undifferentiated 19-sign OR list plus a Stress at work AND gate that the page does not state (page says any sign may indicate substance misuse, stress, depression/anxiety or burnout); 'stress' itself is not encoded as a diagnosis. Omissions: 'Diagnosis of long-term condition' and 'Frequent lateness' are not encoded, and the heavy-drinking concept drops the >=4 drinks past-year threshold.
